title: Choose CYCLEBOOK's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Operator's Manual. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Operator's Manual
options.lineage: Farm-equipment operator's manuals, parts catalogs and load charts
options.thesis: Deere's earnings cycle, documented the way its machines are: numbered figures, specifications and signal words.
options.viewport: PULSE as manual section 01: green thumb tabs down the left edge, FIG. 1-1 exploding Q3 FY26 earnings into numbered parts, and a SPECIFICATIONS sheet with price, market cap and guidance.
options.risk: Tips into costume if the manual devices outnumber the analysis; full green-and-yellow livery can read as a Deere fan page.

raised.raise: Fixed-cell tables: every key-data table keeps the same columns in the same order on every page, and periods never re-sort.
Three inks per page; the one lead figure prints inverted, so rank shows by inversion rather than size.
The active section tab and section band are drenched in field green and own an edge of the page, never sprinkled as accents.
Plots stay achromatic ink; color is spent only on provenance tags and the one series that carries the finding.
MODEL figures carry a diagonal hatch as well as a yellow CAUTION tag, so assumptions separate from actuals in grayscale.

regions.label: running header · section 01 · data as of

options.label: Initiation of Coverage
options.thesis: CYCLEBOOK as the front page of a research note: rating box, key data, numbered exhibits with a source line under each.
options.viewport: A masthead with price and implied value in a rating box, the investment view in running text, and Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 2 stacked at right.
options.risk: Familiar: it is where most finance portfolio pieces land, and it can read as a PDF rather than something to explore.

options.label: Cycle Folio
options.lineage: Botanical folios that follow one plant through the seasons at fixed scale
options.thesis: Peak, compression, trough and recovery drawn as plates at exactly the same scale, so the cycle compares honestly.
options.viewport: Four equal plates across the page, each a phase of the cycle, every segment on one shared axis.
options.case: Holds product clarity (shared-scale small multiples make the cycle exact); loses audience identification, since botanical plates read as neither finance nor Deere.
options.risk: Its cream ground and italic captions are two of the most common AI-generated tells; it needs a different stock to survive.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: Split-flap boards in rail concourses and old trading floors
options.thesis: Quarterly results as board rows: period, segment, status.
options.viewport: A full-width board of quarter rows with fixed columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: rail wayfinding is not the audience's world, and a board cannot carry a valuation chart.
options.kept: Fixed-cell discipline: columns never move, only values change.
options.risk: Power BI cannot animate the flaps, so the board would be a still image of motion.

options.label: Destination Blind
options.lineage: Bus depot destination blinds on dyed cloth
options.thesis: Pages as courses on a cloth roll stepping under one window.
options.viewport: One fixed window showing the current section's course.
options.case: Loses both axes: the metaphor hides the numbers from a reader with ten minutes.
options.kept: Three inks only, with rank shown by inversion.
options.risk: The step motion it depends on is impossible in a report page.

options.label: Seedbed Lobes
options.lineage: Saturated-field product marketing with floating capsule UI
options.thesis: One green field owns the page; everything floats on it as pills.
options.viewport: A green field with a floating pill bar and oversized flush-left headline.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is a startup-marketing grammar, and hiring managers would read it as a landing page.
options.kept: One color owns a whole region instead of being scattered.
options.risk: Reads as SaaS marketing, the opposite of research.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.thesis: An achromatic field with color only at the edges.
options.viewport: Wide white margins with a thin spectral band marking the active item.
options.case: Loses both axes: no connection to Deere or finance, and pastel bands blur provenance.
options.kept: Data fields stay achromatic; color lives only where it means something.
options.risk: Pretty and weightless for a subject that is heavy iron.

options.label: Quoted Industrial
options.lineage: Industrial streetwear labeling and hazard striping
options.thesis: Every label in quotes, hazard stripes under what matters.
options.viewport: Caps labels in straight quotes with diagonal stripes marking modeled values.
options.case: Loses audience identification (fashion irony in a finance read); holds some clarity through literal labels.
options.kept: Hatching marks what is not fact, independent of color.
options.risk: The irony undercuts the credibility a research piece needs.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Power BI finance dashboard as the category ships it, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A row of KPI cards over a revenue trend, a segment chart and a detail table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other finance dashboard by design.
